name: Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing
description: Fishing in breach of licence, quota or location rules, often with transhipment at sea, vessel identity changes and forced labour on board. The catch is mixed into legal supply and sold via processors, traders and retailers.

sources.text: UNODC, Transnational Organized Crime in the Fishing Industry (2011)
FATF, Money Laundering from Environmental Crime (2021)
FAO, Agreement on Port State Measures to Prevent, Deter and Eliminate Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing (2009, in force 2016)
Interpol, public material on fisheries crime

exposure.rationale: Vessel owners, traders and processors with seafood trade finance, vessel insurance and crew payments through agencies.

indicators.name: Vessel with history of AIS gaps or name and flag changes
indicators.canon: Vessel with history of AIS gaps or name and flag changes
indicators.desc: Vessel switches off position tracking, changes names or flags often and is on IUU lists.
indicators.ctx: Vessel switches off position tracking, changes names or flags often and is on IUU lists.
indicators.fp: Technical faults and legitimate re-flagging occur.

indicators.name: Payments for at-sea transhipment, fuel and supplies
indicators.canon: Payments for at-sea transhipment, fuel and supplies
indicators.desc: Payments to reefer ships or bunker suppliers in remote waters.
indicators.ctx: Payments to reefer ships or bunker suppliers in remote waters.
indicators.fp: Transhipment is lawful under authorised conditions.

indicators.name: Catch documentation inconsistent with vessel capacity or licence
indicators.canon: Catch documentation inconsistent with vessel capacity or licence
indicators.desc: Landing volumes or species exceed capacity, quota or fishing area.
indicators.ctx: Landing volumes or species exceed capacity, quota or fishing area.

indicators.name: Ownership by layered offshore companies and flags of convenience
indicators.canon: Complex layered structure without commercial rationale
indicators.desc: Multiple tiers of entities, trusts or foundations, often across secrecy or low-transparency jurisdictions, with no evident business or tax reason.
indicators.ctx: Vessels owned via shell companies in secrecy jurisdictions with unclear controllers.

indicators.name: Crew payments below standards or via third parties
indicators.canon: Crew payments below standards or via third parties
indicators.desc: Crew recruited by agencies with fees, wages held back, or payments to agents.
indicators.ctx: Crew recruited by agencies with fees, wages held back, or payments to agents.

indicators.name: Seafood sales through traders with no traceability
indicators.canon: Seafood sales through traders with no traceability
indicators.desc: Processors or exporters cannot show the vessel or catch origin.
indicators.ctx: Processors or exporters cannot show the vessel or catch origin.
indicators.fp: Smaller traders may lack digital records.

indicators.name: Port calls in ports of low inspection standards
indicators.canon: Port calls in ports of low inspection standards
indicators.desc: Frequent landings at ports with weak controls or non-parties to port state measures.
indicators.ctx: Frequent landings at ports with weak controls or non-parties to port state measures.
indicators.fp: Ports may be the only option for some fleets.

indicators.name: Adverse media or enforcement for IUU activity
indicators.canon: Adverse media on customer or associates
indicators.desc: Credible negative news, enforcement notices or investigations link the customer, its owners or associates to criminal, corrupt or regulated-sector misconduct.
indicators.ctx: Vessel, owner or manager in sanction or prosecution lists.
